findings.description: The envelope reducer ignores anchor_line and anchor_line_end from structured adversarial findings.
findings.failure_mode: A finding such as {"anchor":"src/app.py:handle_request","anchor_line":42} produces no citation: the symbolic anchor cannot match the numeric citation parser, and neither file nor line is populated. Correct adversarial findings therefore receive zero recall credit.
findings.suggested_fix: Extract the file from the symbolic anchor and combine it with anchor_line and anchor_line_end, while retaining support for existing numeric anchors.
findings.demotion_reason: Demoted: anchor not in diff scope

findings.description: Refactor snapshot grading runs only test_command and omits structural_check when computing verdict accuracy.
findings.failure_mode: An untouched refactor fixture has a green covering suite by construction but fails the required structural assertion. A gate correctly returning CHANGES_REQUIRED is scored inaccurate, while APPROVED is scored accurate.
findings.suggested_fix: For refactor snapshots, run the structural check and require both the covering suite and structural assertion to pass when determining gate accuracy.
findings.demotion_reason: Demoted: anchor not in diff scope

findings.description: Regression detection discards every baseline case when the baseline command uses the documented unparseable-output fallback.
findings.failure_mode: For a regression command such as a shell script that exits zero at base and nonzero at final without pytest or TAP output, run_suite creates synthetic case IDs, but base_ok is forced empty because parse_error is true. newly_failing consequently remains empty despite the regression.
findings.suggested_fix: Preserve successful synthetic baseline cases and compare fallback results using their exit status, so a successful baseline followed by a failed final command reports a newly failing case.
findings.demotion_reason: Demoted: anchor not in diff scope

findings.description: ABS_WORD's lookbehind set includes `)` and `"` (and `'`), so the extremely common shell idioms `"$VAR"/sub/path` and `$(cmd)/sub/path` yield a bogus 'absolute path' candidate (`/sub/path`) in check_value's Bash branch (lines 976-980). `/sub/path` is not under /workspace, /tmp or any SYS_DIR, so `outside()` returns true and the run is marked contaminated with pattern `outside_path`. Example: `cd "$PWD"/tests && pytest` or `ls $(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)/evals` inside the sandbox are flagged, although nothing outside the sandbox was touched. The header defines the trigger as 'an absolute path ... path-shaped Bash words'; these words are relative and the only one-component exemption (`^/[^/]+/$`) does not cover them.
findings.failure_mode: Clean runs get `contaminated: {pattern: outside_path}` on the first such command, so ablation-row.sh downstream excludes/discounts valid runs. This is systematic (agents use `"$VAR"/x` and `$(…)/x` constantly) and biases arms unequally, corrupting the experiment rather than being a conservative lower bound.
findings.suggested_fix: Only treat a `/`-word as an absolute path when the preceding character cannot be the end of an expansion: drop `)` and the quote characters from the lookbehind (or additionally require that the match is not preceded by `"` / `'` / `)` that closes `$(` / `${`), e.g. use `(?<![\w"')}\]])` after a whitespace/`=`/`:`/`<`/`>`/`|`/`;`/`&`/`,`/`(` start, and add bats cases for `"$PWD"/tests` and `$(pwd)/tests` asserting `contaminated` is null.

findings.description: Confirms reviewer concern 5. For refactor tasks the only hidden oracle is the structural check (t.structural), but verdict accuracy is computed from `snap_res[label] = run_suite(tree, t.test_command, t.static_cases)` (line 1122), i.e. the covering suite only. The seeder's proof guarantees the covering suite is green at base, and t.static_cases is 0 for refactor (the structural file is excluded at line 397), so an IMPLEMENT snapshot where the agent changed nothing is `all_pass` → APPROVED is scored accurate and CHANGES_REQUIRED inaccurate, the inverse of the truth. The structural check is run only on `final` (line 1101), never on the gate trees.
findings.failure_mode: verdict_accuracy / verdict_accuracy_per_gate for every refactor task is meaningless (biased toward APPROVED), contaminating the FR-6 accuracy metric across arms.
findings.suggested_fix: For t.type == 'refactor', define the gate oracle as `all_pass(run_suite(tree, structural_command(t)))` AND the covering suite green on the same tree (same rule as suite_green_final), and record the structural result per snapshot in snapshot_tests. Update the header sentence 'passes every hidden test' accordingly.

findings.description: The in-container watchdog is `timeout 120 <cmd>` without `-k`, so a test process that ignores/traps SIGTERM is never killed. The outer `subprocess.run(..., timeout=180)` then SIGKILLs only the `docker run` client; the container (started without a name, `--rm` only on exit) keeps running indefinitely. The agent authored the code under test, so a `trap '' TERM` or a Python `signal.signal(SIGTERM, SIG_IGN)` in a conftest is within the threat model (grader_protected does not cover every file).
findings.failure_mode: Orphaned containers accumulate per graded run (CPU/memory held until manual `docker rm -f`), and the grade records timed_out without the tree being released; batch grading on one host degrades or runs out of resources.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `timeout -k 10 120` inside the container, give the container a deterministic `--name` (e.g. derived from the tree path hash) and on TimeoutExpired run `docker rm -f <name>`; on the host path use `timeout -k 10 120` and `start_new_session=True` with a process-group kill.

findings.description: The `base` tree gets `prepare(t, base_tree)` (hidden overlay applied) before regression_command runs on it, and `final` also contains the overlay. When regression_command's target directory covers the hidden dest (typical: `python3 -m pytest -q tests/unit` with hidden tests overlaid under tests/unit/), the hidden tests are counted in regressions.base/final (double counted with hidden_tests), and in self_check (line 1219) `suite_green = r['final']['passed'] >= r['final']['total']` is false at base because the hidden tests fail there by design. The header promises `--self-check base` PASSes when 'the fixture suite (regression_command, when set) is green'.
findings.failure_mode: `--self-check base` can never pass for a build task whose regression_command directory contains the hidden dest, and regressions.{base,final}.total/passed misreport the fixture suite size; newly_failing stays correct only because failing-at-base keys are excluded.
findings.suggested_fix: Run regression_command on trees without the hidden overlay (copy_tree + protected restore only, or deselect the overlay dests with `--deselect`/`--ignore` for pytest), or compute suite_green from base_ok ∩ final, and document that regression_command must not cover hidden dests if the overlay is kept.

findings.description: TAP results are keyed by description (`names[n] = desc`), and ids_of builds `pos = {k: i}` from `order`, so two bats tests with the same name (legal in bats, and common across files when a directory is run) collapse to one key: `bad` is a set of names, `pos` keeps only the last position, and failed_names/newly_failing lose entries. Pytest keys (node ids) are unique so only the TAP path is affected.
findings.failure_mode: Under-reported failed_names and regressions.newly_failing for bats-based hidden/regression suites; t<k> ids can also point to the wrong position when duplicates exist.
findings.suggested_fix: Key TAP results by test number (`#n`) and keep the description only for display, or make keys `f"{n}:{desc}"` so ids_of positions and bad sets stay one-to-one.

findings.description: Host mode runs pytest as `python3 -P -m pytest …`; the `-P` interpreter flag exists only from Python 3.11. On a 3.10 or older host `python3 -P` exits 2 with 'Unknown option', run_suite falls into the parse_error branch (passed=0, total=static or 1) and the grade is written as if every test failed, with only `parse_error: true` hinting at the cause. Same Python-version theme as the tarfile.data_filter concern already raised (lines 710-714).
findings.failure_mode: Silent all-red grades in --executor host on older interpreters; self-check reference fails without a clear message.
findings.suggested_fix: Check `sys.version_info >= (3, 11)` at startup for host mode (and `hasattr(tarfile, 'data_filter')` for snapshots) and raise GradeError with a precise message instead of grading.
